rule: A command is the whole message, in any letter case. The clone's icon written on its own anywhere in it is left out, so a command may carry it. Anything else is ordinary conversation.

senders.description: The person whose clone it is.
Anyone in the workspace but the owner.

places.description: The owner's direct message to themselves in Slack.
A colleague's one-to-one DM with the owner.
Any conversation the clone hears, with the clone's icon in the message.

commands.effect: The clone answers you only when you call it with its icon.
The clone treats you like everyone else again. While it soft-ignores you, write the clone's icon in the message too, or the message never reaches it.

For 14 days, or until hands on, the clone answers nobody else in one place: in a thread, that thread; in a channel's main conversation, the thread under your message; in a DM's main conversation, that conversation but not its threads. What others wrote there that waits for it is dropped. Your own messages with the clone's icon still reach it. Write the icon in the command, or the clone never sees it. Refused in your self-DM.

The clone may answer others again in the place hands off named, the one this message is in: the same thread, or a DM's main conversation. Write the clone's icon in the command, or the clone never sees it.

The clone stops answering the person: their messages no longer reach it as something to answer, they can't call it, and what of theirs waits for it is dropped. It can still see their messages in a thread or conversation it reads to answer someone else, and nothing they wrote is deleted.
The clone answers the person only when they call it with its icon.
The clone treats the person like everyone else again, whether it ignored or soft-ignored them.
The people named may ask the clone for work besides you: tickets, implementation and reviews.
The clone reads every message in the channels named, and answers what asks something of you or your work.
Workers may merge reviewed pull requests in the repository. Refused for a repository your settings don't list.
Workers stop at a reviewed pull request in the repository. Refused for a repository your settings don't list.
The clone keeps your words as your next numbered note.
commands.example: remember Releases go out on Tuesdays.

commands.effect: The clone's next message starts a new Claude session. The old session's transcript stays, and so do your settings and notes.

Misha pauses: the clone tries to stop its workers, starts nothing new and answers only your commands in your self-DM until you resume. It still sees what arrives in Slack. A worker it could not stop may still run: Home names it, and you stop it by hand.
The clone answers with your settings: its icon, personality, who it ignores, who may ask for work, the channels it watches, where workers merge, and your notes.
